hero.headline: A {{Real Fly Brain}} Is Answering Your Questions Right Now
hero.subheadline: A real fly's wiring map — 165,000 neurons — simulated live. Ask anything with a yes-or-no answer and watch which way it turns.

ask.helper: One yes/no question, up to 140 characters. Every question gets its turn, even if the line is long.
rules: Yes/no questions only, 140 characters max, no links or @handles
No named private individuals, no voting how-to, no medical or financial advice
Up to 3 questions in line per person
The same words always get the same answer: a repeat is shown at once, marked as asked before

rejected_messages.not_yes_no: That's not a yes/no question. Rephrase it so the fly only has two ways to turn.
rejected_messages.voting_procedure: We keep the fly away from voting logistics: how, where, or when to vote. Your county elections office has that answer.
rejected_messages.medical: No medical questions. A fly's nervous system isn't a doctor, and neither is this page.
rejected_messages.financial_advice: Not financial advice, and we won't let the fly play at giving any. Try a different question.
rejected_messages.private_person: No questions about named private individuals. Public figures and public events only.
rejected_messages.violence_or_hate: That question doesn't clear moderation. Try something else.
rejected_messages.sexual: Keep it non-sexual. The fly's courtship circuits are for the science, not for this.
rejected_messages.spam: Looks like spam or a duplicate. One real question at a time.
rejected_messages.too_long: 140 characters max, shorter than that tweet you didn't send.
rejected_messages.rate_limited: You've asked enough for now. Give the queue a minute and try again.
rejected_messages.captcha: Quick check first: prove you're not a bot before a real brain answers you.

ask.disclaimer: Your question is published on this page as soon as it is accepted — don't include personal details. Answers are for entertainment and research, not advice.

appetite.label: Appetite
appetite.tooltip: Fired MN9, the motor neuron that extends a fly's proboscis to feed. Reads as reaching toward something, not literal hunger.

fear.label: Startle
fear.tooltip: Fired the giant fiber circuit (DNp01), the fast pathway behind a fly's escape jump. Reads as flinching away, not a felt emotion.

backoff.label: Backed off
backoff.tooltip: Fired the MDN "moonwalker" neurons that drive backward walking. Reads as retreating from the question.

courtship.label: Courtship
courtship.tooltip: Fired P1/pC1 and pIP10, the circuits behind courtship song and display in male flies. Reads as strong engagement, not romantic interest.

arousal.label: Whole-brain buzz
arousal.tooltip: How much of the entire brain lit up, not one circuit. Reads as how hard the question landed, not how the fly feels about it.

answer.caveat: The fly reacts to the pattern of your words, not their meaning.

how_it_works.title: You ask
how_it_works.body: Type a yes/no question. A small tool, not the fly and not a chatbot, turns your words into numbers.

how_it_works.title: Numbers become a signal
how_it_works.body: Those numbers set a pattern of activity on real sensory neurons: taste, smell, sight and touch, the way an actual flavor or smell would.

how_it_works.title: The whole brain runs
how_it_works.body: All ~165,000 neurons of a male fruit fly's brain and nerve cord fire for a quarter of a second, wired as scientists mapped it in the real animal (Janelia MaleCNS v1.0).

how_it_works.title: The turn is the answer
how_it_works.body: Whichever side the signal reaches the fly's motor-command neurons harder decides which way it turns. Left or right maps to yes or no.

how_it_works.title: You see the real spikes
how_it_works.body: Every neuron that fired lights up on the page and the stream, placed at its real position in the brain, along with any named behavior program (feeding, escape, courtship) it triggered.

how_it_works.title: It doesn't understand the question
how_it_works.body: The fly has no idea what a market, a match or a person is. That's the honest part: we're testing whether real brain wiring produces a structured response at all, not simulating understanding.

honesty.title: What this {{actually is, and isn't}}
honesty.body: The only machine-learning step here is small: a text-embedding model turns your words into numbers. It doesn't write anything and it doesn't choose your answer. Those numbers become a sensory signal into a real, complete connectome, the full wiring diagram of a male fruit fly's brain and nerve cord, and a biophysical simulation runs the whole thing, spike by spike, for a quarter of a second. The fly's own wiring decides which way it turns, not any AI. It has no idea what your question means. We show the real spike pattern next to every answer, because that's the actual honesty check: does real brain wiring respond differently from a scrambled one, or not.

about_lab.title: IG Digital Lab: a {{digital-brain research lab}}
about_lab.body: IG Digital Lab is an AI and software company in Sacramento, California. Our team builds AI into how businesses work: custom software, AI workflow automation, AI for calls and chat, websites and apps. BioReservoir is our research lab. Each time a new brain-wiring map is published (a fly today, maybe a rat or a primate next), we build an experiment on it, publish the method, and score every result against real controls.
